Rules / Performance

SK4004 Review boxing despite an existing generic constraint

An explicit interface cast boxes a value-type-constrained type parameter before an interface method call, despite an existing matching constraint.

CategoryPerformance
Default severityhint
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3

Why

A constrained generic call can often dispatch without boxing. An explicit cast to the already-provided interface introduces a boxing conversion. Removing it is not automatically safe: a mutating struct method may then modify the original value instead of the boxed copy, and overload selection can differ.

Example

Instead of:

int M<T>(T value, T other) where T : struct, IComparable<T> => ((IComparable<T>)value).CompareTo(other);

Write:

int M<T>(T value, T other) where T : struct, IComparable<T> => value.CompareTo(other); // after reviewing copy semantics

When it does not fire

Only explicit boxing casts immediately used as an interface method receiver are reported. The source must be a type parameter constrained to a value type and to the target interface, directly or through an inherited interface. Reference-type and unconstrained generic casts, object casts, extension methods, retained boxes, interface property access and expression trees are excluded. The rule identifies a boxing conversion, not an exact runtime allocation count; JIT optimization and deliberate copy semantics can make retaining it appropriate. No automatic fix is offered.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK4004.severity
